summary: Proposes conventions for using an IBM 2741 typewriter-style terminal to log in to ARPANET server hosts. The 2741 can key in 92 different codes, but a few of them, such as the cent sign and the new-line key, have no direct ASCII equivalent, so the note suggests how to map them. RFC 135 responded with a different set of conventions.

eli5.summary: A special typewriter has a few keys that other computers do not understand. This note decides what those keys should turn into, like agreeing that a smiley key means a colon and a bracket.

questions: how to use an ibm 2741 terminal on the arpanet
how were 2741 keys mapped to ascii
